title: Club Arlington's name, Tom Anderson and Decatur Street
summary: Talk of Tom Anderson, Josie Arlington and how Decatur Street held all the clubs.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Do you know who Arlington was? Did you meet anyone named Arlington?
No. I don't know why the club was named Arlington Club, but that's what the name of the club was.
Well, Tom Anderson used to have that club yesterday.
Yeah. I've got pictures I've seen of him. Yeah, I've got pictures of him. You know who he was? Tom Anderson? Yeah, he was. I remember the name of the... He ran the red light district.
Well, if that's... He was kind of Heverset, dude. I think he did. Big mustache.

I've got a picture of him. Because he had that club, he was operating that club, and he had a club on wood. He was operating that club on wood. And Andrew Anderson was working at the club on wood. And Andrew Anderson was working at the club on wood. And we was at the club all on the thing. Yeah, well he was tied up with Josie Arlington. And she had a house, you know. She was in that space line. So he was all tied up with that. What was Decatur Street like then? Decatur Street was Wood.
Mm-hm. Decatur Street was Boorman Street. Mm-hm. Boorman Street wasn't no one. Yeah. It wasn't nothing. Decatur Street was everything. All the club was right there on Decatur Street.

Wilming Street wasn't on it. Wasn't nothing. Wasn't a thing on Wilming Street. Decairn Street was everything. All the clubs was right there on Decairn Street. But it was rough. It was a rough place to go on Decairn Street.
